coreIdea: Loop-count as summations; nested loops multiply; log-dividing/multiplying loops = Θ(log n). Comparison-bound problems = recall classical tight results.
mustRememberFormulas: Triangular nested loop (i to n) is still Θ(n²), half the constant of full n×n
Max-finding: n-1 comparisons (tight). Max+Min together: ⌈3n/2⌉-2 (tight, beats naive 2n)
Comparison sort lower bound: Ω(n log n)
Exponentiation by squaring: x^n in O(log n) multiplications, not O(n)

patternRecognitionTable.seeThis: loop-heavy code, asked for time complexity/operation count

recursive function, asked for time complexity

commonTrapsQuickList: Triangular nested loops are Θ(n²), not a lower class
Don't confuse an achievable comparison count (upper bound) with the PROVEN minimum (tight lower bound)
x^n needs O(log n) multiplications via squaring, not O(n)
Naive doubling-recursive functions (calling themselves twice) are exponential — memoization fixes it to polynomial
highYieldPyqLessons: Comparison-bound problems (10/31) are the single biggest sub-skill — build a mental library of classical tight bounds (max, max+min, sorting) rather than re-deriving each time.
Loop-derivation (7/31) rewards writing an explicit summation over eyeballing — always write Σ before answering.
